acceptance.given: A destructive operation is being defined or requested under SM-A16.

oracle.expected: The operation declaration identifies the confirmation or authorization source required for execution.
forbidden: The declaration omits the required confirmation or authorization source.
oracle.observable: Static evaluation of the operation declaration finds an explicit confirmation or authorization source associated with that operation.

acceptance.then: The static check identifies the declared source for the operation.
acceptance.when: The SM-A16 package check evaluates the destructive-operation declaration.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select an SM-A16 destructive-operation declaration with no confirmation or authorization source and run the applicable package check.

affected_subjects: Destructive operation confirmation or authorization source
slice_hint.behavior_change: Require destructive-operation declarations to identify the confirmation or authorization source, and make the static check evaluate that declaration.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Documentation and static package-check rule only; no persisted state or schema migration.

slice_hint.state_transition: The declaration is evaluated for its source; absent source is rejected and a present source continues through validation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A targeted check distinguishes a declaration that names the required source from one that omits it.

acceptance.given: A destructive operation has an existing session or user authorization that the owning policy defines as valid.

oracle.expected: Authorization evaluation accepts the existing session or user authorization and proceeds with the operation.
forbidden: A policy-accepted existing authorization is rejected solely because it is not newly supplied.
A different source is demanded although the owning policy accepts the existing authorization.
oracle.observable: The authorization evaluation result indicates that the existing policy-approved authorization satisfies the operation's authorization requirement.

acceptance.then: The authorization evaluation accepts the existing authorization and continues the operation flow.
acceptance.when: The operation authorization rule is evaluated against the existing session or user authorization.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select an operation whose owning policy accepts the existing session or user authorization and assert that evaluation rejects it or requires a different source.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Honor an owning policy's acceptance of existing session or user authorization for destructive operations.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Authorization policy interpretation only; no persisted state or schema migration.

slice_hint.state_transition: A policy-approved existing authorization satisfies the authorization requirement and allows the operation flow to continue.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A targeted authorization check accepts an existing source when the owning policy marks it valid.

acceptance.given: The owning policy accepts an existing session or user authorization for the destructive operation.

oracle.expected: The authorization flow does not impose an additional confirmation solely as a universal extra step once the existing authorization satisfies the owning policy.
forbidden: Every destructive operation is forced through redundant confirmation regardless of policy.
Additional confirmation is required after the existing authorization satisfies the owning policy.
oracle.observable: Evaluation of the authorization flow shows no extra confirmation requirement inserted after the existing authorization has satisfied policy.

acceptance.then: The authorization flow continues without a redundant confirmation requirement.
acceptance.when: The operation flow evaluates whether another confirmation is required after applying the owning policy.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select an operation with policy-accepted existing authorization and assert that the flow imposes an additional confirmation solely as a universal requirement.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Do not impose an additional universal confirmation when policy-accepted existing authorization already satisfies the operation's requirement.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Authorization policy interpretation only; policies that separately require confirmation remain expressible.

slice_hint.state_transition: After accepted existing authorization, the flow proceeds without entering a redundant-confirmation requirement.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A targeted check confirms the accepted existing authorization does not trigger an additional universal confirmation requirement.

acceptance.given: A capability uses a runtime credential.

oracle.expected: The capability definition or related documentation names a safe credential-reference mechanism.
forbidden: A capability uses a runtime credential without naming a safe reference mechanism.
oracle.observable: Static inspection of the capability definition or its related documentation locates the named safe credential-reference mechanism.

acceptance.then: The capability's safe credential-reference mechanism is identified by the static check.
acceptance.when: The SM-A15 package check evaluates the capability's runtime-credential declaration.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a capability declaration that uses a runtime credential but omits its safe credential-reference mechanism, then run the applicable SM-A15 package check.

affected_subjects: 使用运行时凭据的能力
slice_hint.behavior_change: Require capabilities using runtime credentials to name a safe credential-reference mechanism and validate that declaration statically.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Static authoring and package-check rule only; no credential persistence or schema migration.

slice_hint.state_transition: A credential-using capability declaration is evaluated for its safe reference mechanism; missing metadata is rejected.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A targeted check distinguishes a capability that names its safe reference mechanism from one that omits it.
